summary: @onereach/idw-sdk preinstall drops Bun runtime and auto-executes an obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that runs on `npm install`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style hex identifiers and constant-property lookup wrappers (`_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`, `YCZJE`, `QkQej`, `TdVzu`) that hide its strings and control flow. On install the script probes the host, and if Bun is not already installed it downloads a Bun runtime archive from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<platform>.zip` into a temp directory, unpacks it, chmods it executable, then invokes that freshly dropped Bun binary against a sibling file `math_init.js` via `execFileSync`. If Bun is already present, that Bun is used to execute `math_init.js` directly. `math_init.js` is a ~727 KB Bun-compiled file (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) with string-array-rotator obfuscation (`WV8StW` rotating a large mixed array; randomized identifiers such as `MmgoCP`, `JqTtnbZ`, `hc1jfK9`) that makes the payload body deliberately unreadable to Node-based reviewers and scanners. The package's advertised purpose is a typed axios HTTP client for the IDW API, which has no need to fetch a second JavaScript runtime at install time or to ship a large obfuscated Bun-compiled artifact. The combination — obfuscated preinstall dropper + alternate-runtime fetch + auto-execution of an opaque bundled payload — is an install-time remote code execution surface running on every installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
